data: NASA's medium-lift planetary-science workhorse 1989-2018 — Dawn, Messenger, MRO, Phoenix, Kepler

Two- or three-stage liquid-LOX/RP-1 first stage (Rocketdyne RS-27A) with up to nine GEM-40 / GEM-46 strap-on SRBs and a Star-48B solid-kick third stage for high-energy missions. 155 launches 1989-02-14 (Navstar II-1) through 2018-09-15 (ICESat-2), with a 98.7% success rate (153 of 155) that made it NASA's go-to for planetary probes too heavy for Pegasus and too light to justify Atlas / Delta IV. The 7000-series evolved out of the post-Challenger GPS requirement; the 7920H + Star-48B 'Delta II Heavy' variant launched Dawn (2007) and Messenger (2004). Retired after the company merged its medium-lift line into Atlas V + Falcon 9.

Two- or three-stage Delta variant with an RS-27A LOX/RP-1 first stage, up to nine GEM strap-on solid boosters, and an optional Star-48B kick stage for high-energy escape trajectories. 155 launches over 29 years with a 98.7% success rate; carried Dawn, Messenger, MRO, Phoenix, Kepler, Spitzer, GRAIL, and the original GPS Block II constellation. The 'Delta II Heavy' (7920H + Star-48B) was the configuration that delivered enough C3 for direct-to-Ceres + Mercury orbital insertion. Retired after the medium-lift market shifted to Atlas V and Falcon 9.
First wheels on Mars; demonstrated airbag landing
First of the Mars Exploration Rover twins; longest-lived rover until passed by Opportunity
Held the Mars driving record (45.16 km) until Perseverance passed it in October 2026; 14-year surface lifetime against a 90-sol design
First spacecraft to orbit Mercury; first complete surface map of the innermost planet
First mission to orbit two extraterrestrial bodies — Vesta, then Ceres
First confirmation of water ice in the Martian arctic regolith; first soft propulsive Mars landing since Viking 2
Twin to Spirit; nearly 15-year Mars operation
First Mercury orbiter — 6 planetary gravity assists over 6.6 years to bleed energy before insertion in 2011
Only spacecraft to orbit two extraterrestrial worlds — Vesta then Ceres via ion propulsion
Confirmed water ice in Martian soil
1970s NASA outer-planet workhorse — Pioneer 10/11, Helios 1/2, Mariner 9/10, Pioneer Venus
Lifted Apollo 7, Skylab crews, and ASTP
The last Delta II, built from leftover flight hardware, in the Rocket Garden
